gift.title: Christmas quest: Torun
gift.text: In December Torun smells of honey, cinnamon and cloves, and gingerbread has been baked here since the 14th century. The quest "The Gingerbread City Under the First Star" is a kilometer and a half through the Old and New Town: from the Franciscan church across the Market Square to the gingerbread museums. For centuries two Christmases lived side by side here — with a tree for some and the first star for others.

gift.title: Dictionary of Kalyady
gift.text: Kalyady has a language of its own. Shchodrukha, the Goat, the hungry kutia — do you know what stands behind each word? Match the word with its meaning. All the facts come from our Christmas quests in Belarus, and the most “Kalyady” of them is the one in Gomel: twelve days of holidays on a single street.

task.text: Make six “word — meaning” pairs.

pairs.right: Generous Evening in the Brest region
pairs.fact: On Shchodrukha pancakes were always baked, and carolers were given a pancake brushed with butter or lard. From the Brest quest.

pairs.right: A costumed figure in a sheepskin coat, fur outward
pairs.fact: The Goat danced at the threshold, fell down exhausted and came back to life only when the host brought out sausage, lard or pancakes. From the Brest quest.

pairs.right: A fasting supper on the eve of Epiphany
pairs.fact: At Christmastide three kutias were laid out: a lenten one before Christmas, a rich one with meat on Generous Evening, and the “hungry”, watery one. From the Gomel quest.

pairs.right: A memory of the Infant's manger
pairs.fact: It, together with the lenten kutia, the first of the three Christmas ones, opened the Christmas evening. From the Minsk quest.

pairs.right: A midnight Mass in honor of the shepherds
pairs.fact: The shepherds were the first to come to the manger. People gather for pasterka before midnight between 24 and 25 December. From the Brest quest.

pairs.right: The villain of the batlejka's lower tier
pairs.fact: At the top of the box the puppets played out the Nativity, below Herod ruled with his soldiers, costumed figures and devils. From the Minsk quest.

gift.title: Who comes at Christmas?
gift.text: In every corner of Poland a different guest comes at Christmas: one with a sack and a rod, one invisible, one riding a white horse. Match the guest with his region. All the facts come from our Christmas quests, and the place to start is Poznan, where Gwiazdor knocks at the door.

task.text: Make six “guest — region” pairs.

pairs.left: Gwiazdor in a sheepskin coat, fur outward, with a sack and a rod
pairs.fact: Good children get apples, nuts and gingerbread, lazy ones a rod or a pair of “pyry” — potatoes, Poznan-style. From the Poznan quest.

pairs.left: The Little Angel, who cannot be seen
pairs.fact: While the family sits down to Wigilia, he quietly leaves parcels under the tree and vanishes. From the Rzeszow quest.
Before midnight people hurry here to the Pasterka: whoever makes it will have a lucky year. From the Katowice quest.

pairs.left: The white horse Szemel at the head of the costumed troupe

gift.title: A traveler's Christmas story
gift.text:
Just before Christmas a traveler was walking through the forest to the station and missed the last train. A blizzard was burying the rails, and his phone had died. At the edge of the village one window was lit, and on the sill stood a candle: by an old custom it is set out on Christmas Eve so that anyone on the road knows they are expected here.

The door was opened at once. They poured him hot tea, set an extra plate and asked him nothing. In the morning the blizzard died down. On leaving, the traveler left his road map on the windowsill with the note "I was expected here".

They say that since then every route of his has one point with no name. He stops there every winter.

gift.title: Whose custom is this?
gift.text: Christmas and New Year are welcomed in different ways: somewhere people eat grapes as the clock strikes midnight, somewhere they give books and read them that same evening. Match the custom to the country.

task.text: Make six "custom — country" pairs.

pairs.left: 12 grapes with the 12 strokes of the clock at New Year's midnight
pairs.fact: Each grape stands for a month of the new year. Managing to eat all twelve brings good luck.

pairs.left: Giving books on Christmas Eve and reading them that same evening
pairs.fact: The book season here is called the "book flood": since 1944 a catalog of new books has arrived at every home.

pairs.left: A star lantern, the parol, on every house
pairs.fact: San Fernando hosts a festival of giant lanterns, up to 12 meters across.

pairs.left: The witch Befana brings gifts on the night of 6 January
pairs.fact: Sweets for good children, a lump of coal for naughty ones. Usually a sugar one.

pairs.left: A little spider on the Christmas tree brings happiness
pairs.fact: Legend has it that a spider wove a web around a poor widow's tree overnight, and in the morning the sun turned the web into gold and silver.

pairs.left: An extra plate at the Wigilia supper for an unexpected guest
pairs.fact: The empty seat awaits any traveler who knocks on Christmas Eve.

gift.title: Kutia (kuccia) for the Christmas table
gift.text:
Kutia (kuccia in Belarusian) is a barley porridge with honey and poppy seeds. The name covers both the dish and the supper on Christmas Eve.

You will need:
— barley groats — 200 g
— water — 700 ml
— poppy seeds — 3 tbsp
— honey — 3 tbsp
— raisins — 50 g
— walnuts — 50 g
— salt — a pinch

How to make it:
1. Pour boiling water over the poppy seeds, leave for an hour, drain and crush.
2. Add the groats to boiling salted water and simmer for 10–15 minutes on low heat.
3. Steep the raisins in boiling water; toast and chop the walnuts.
4. Stir the poppy seeds, honey and raisins into the warm porridge.
5. Wrap the pot in a towel for 30 minutes and sprinkle with walnuts before serving.

gift.title: Toruń-style gingerbread (homemade take)
gift.text:
Toruń gingerbread has been known since the 14th century: the first baker is mentioned in the city in 1380. This is a homemade take on it — not "the real thing", but it smells just as festive.

You will need:
— wheat flour — 500 g
— honey — 200 g
— butter — 150 g
— icing sugar — 100 g
— egg — 1
— baking soda — 1 tsp
— gingerbread spice mix — 1 sachet (or a pinch each of cinnamon, ginger and cloves)

How to make it:
1. Warm the honey, butter, icing sugar and spices on low heat, then cool to lukewarm.
2. Mix the flour with the soda, add the egg and the honey mixture, and knead a dough.
3. Chill the dough in the fridge for 2 hours.
4. Roll it out 3–4 mm thick, cut out shapes and place them on baking paper.
5. Bake at 180 °C for 8–10 minutes, cool and decorate with icing.

gift.title: Christmastide fortune-telling
gift.text:
Merry Christmas! In Warmia the twelve days after Christmas were considered prophetic: the weather of each one was used to predict what the matching month of the new year would be like. And in the Brest region on Shchodrukha girls carried a pancake out into the street and listened for which side a dog would bark from — that is where a matchmaker would come from.

Our fortune-telling is kinder and about roads: draw a card and it will name your month of 2027. Thank you for being with us all December.

task.text: Draw a card — it will name your travel month of 2027.

items: Your month is January. The first trip of the year will take place on fresh snow, and you will remember that crunch underfoot until spring.
Your month is February. A short weekend trip will turn out bigger than any vacation: so much you will manage to see.
Your month is March. The last snow in the mountains and the first sun in the city — you will catch both on a single trip.
Your month is April. An old manor park will only just be waking up, and you will be the first one in it.
Your month is May. The road will call unexpectedly. Say yes: you haven't had a May like this in a long time.
Your month is June. You will meet the longest day of the year not at home but where the sunset is in no hurry.
Your month is July. A lake with clear water, a tent and silence — in summer everything falls into place by itself.
Your month is August. A meteor shower will catch you on the road. Wish on a falling star for your next trip.
Your month is September. A warm autumn will give you back the route you didn't have time for in summer.
Your month is October. Golden avenues and tea from a thermos: you will take the best shot of the year then.
Your month is November. While everyone sits at home, you will find a city without queues or tourists, all to yourself.
Your month is December. Lights, a market and the smell of gingerbread: you will open next Advent already on the road.
